newsitem.title: USA: Philadelphia tax lien sale expected to pass.
newsitem.headline: Philadelphia tax lien sale expected to pass.

text.p: Philadelphia's City Council is expected to approve Thursday a tax lien sale after heavy lobbying by Mayor Ed Rendeall, according to council observers.
The lien sale is part of a plan to issue about $75 million of bonds backed by delinquent tax collections, with proceeds split between the city and its school district.

The plan involves turning over delinquent tax collections to private agencies, an idea that spooked some council members fearful that aggressive collection tactics would force poor constituents out of their homes.
Rendell convinced wavering council members by agreeing to a $1 million fund to assist working class unemployed residents having trouble paying the tax bill.
